title: Storegga Slide and tsunami
summary: The Storegga Slide, a submarine landslide off the Norwegian coast, displaced a sediment volume of 2400 to 3200 km³ over c. 95 000 km² of seabed. Its tsunami, about 8,150 calendar years ago, left deposits at least 20 m above the sea level of the time in Shetland, 10–12 m in western Norway and 1.5–5.5 m in Denmark.

uncertainty.note: Source states "about 8,150 calendar years ago"; converted with year = 1950 - 8150 = -6200, assuming calendar BP means before 1950. The plus/minus of 100 years is a placeholder for "about", not a sourced figure. Wikidata lists the event as 6225-6170 BCE.

importance.justification: One of the largest mapped Holocene submarine slides, with a tsunami recorded across the North Sea.
